- codebase-memory: Use the codebase knowledge graph for structural code queries. Triggers on: explore the codebase, understand the architecture, what functions exist, show me the structure, who calls this function, what does X call, trace the call chain, find callers of, show dependencies, impact analysis, dead code, unused functions, high fan-out, refactor candidates, code quality audit, graph query syntax, Cypher query examples, edge types, how to use search_graph.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). content.text:
r02.

**Premise correction: this repository has no per-user API rate-limiting middleware.** Memos (this repo) ships no rate limiter at all — no per-user, per-IP, or global request-rate throttling — so there is nowhere it is "registered" and there are no request limits to report.

What I checked:

- **Echo middleware chain** — `server/server.go:51-52` registers only `middleware.Recover()` and `newCORSMiddleware(profile)` (`server/cors.go:13`). The frontend service adds only static-file and SPA-fallback middleware (`server/router/frontend/frontend.go:54,59`).
- **Connect/gRPC interceptors** — `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:133-137` registers exactly four: `NewMetadataInterceptor`, `NewLoggingInterceptor`, `NewRecoveryInterceptor`, `NewAuthInterceptor` (all defined in `server/router/api/v1/connect_interceptors.go`, auth in `server/router/api/v1/auth_service.go`/`authz.go`). None does rate limiting.
- **gRPC-Gateway** — the only gateway middleware is `gatewayAuthMiddleware` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:69,97`).
- **Dependencies** — no rate-limiting library is imported. `golang.org/x/time` appears in `go.mod:151` but is marked `// indirect` and `rate.Limiter` is never used in the codebase.
- **Repo-wide search** for `rate limit`/`throttle` in Go sources returns nothing; the only hits are aspirational docs in `internal/email/doc.go:86` ("Rate limit email sending to prevent abuse", listed as a suggestion) and an illustrative snippet in `internal/email/README.md:291-295` that is example prose, not compiled code.

The limits that do exist are **size/pagination caps, not rate limits**:

- `maxAPIRequestBytes = 256 << 20` (256 MiB) applied via `http.MaxBytesHandler` to `/api/v1/*`, `/file/*`, and the Connect mux, plus `connect.WithReadMaxBytes` — `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:20,126,141,144`.
- Attachment upload cap: `MaxUploadBufferSizeBytes = 32 << 20`, overridden by the instance-level `UploadSizeLimitMb` setting — `server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go:27,120-124`.
- Page-size cap `MaxPageSize` — `server/router/api/v1/common.go:48-52`.
- Memo `contentLengthLimit` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:105,443`.
- A concurrency semaphore of 3 for thumbnail generation — `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:59` (limits parallelism, not request rate).

If you want per-user rate limiting, the natural insertion point is a new Connect interceptor added to the list at `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:133-137` (after `NewAuthInterceptor`, so the user identity is available), mirrored by an Echo middleware in `server/server.go` for the gateway/REST path.
